answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the timber reward in the copper ledger costs the operator directly, and the thread audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 22% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the farming party's own capital. A farm of 114 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
